headline: Meta's careers copy pitches world-scale human connection and bold speed—with DEI language that surged through 2021 and has since quietly receded.
identity: Meta has consistently valued moving fast, building at civilizational scale, and framing individual work as a contribution to global human connection—phrases like 'We're determined to build a better, more connected world for everyone' and 'the pace is fast and the challenges are enormous' recur across nearly every era. Belonging and diversity language was added as a third pillar around 2013, peaked sharply in 2020–2021 (inclusion z-scores of +1.83 and +1.60, with copy like 'Building a diverse team where everyone belongs is crucial'), then retreated: by 2023–2024 the DEI register collapsed to thin 'belonging_culture' framing with no explicit demographic or structural-process language, and the 2026 snapshot shows inclusion scores near the bottom of the peer distribution (z-score –2.06). Techno-optimism, nearly absent from 2011–2022, has surged back in 2025–2026 as the copy pivots to AI, AR glasses, and the metaverse.
fit: You might be a good fit if you are energized by very large, fast-moving problems—the copy consistently reaches for people who 'get excited by big questions and unsolved problems,' want to 'ship things that are not just good, but also awe-inspiring,' and are comfortable with a 'self-starter culture' where 'the pace is fast and the challenges are enormous'; the most recent pages add an explicit AI/hardware frontier angle, so comfort with that domain is increasingly foregrounded.

sections.heading: Speed and Scale as the Constant Core
sections.body:
From the earliest archived copy (2009: 'we move fast and don't mess around') through the 2023 rebrand ('we build and learn faster than anyone else'), performance and impact language has been the most stable signal in Meta's recruiting pages. The performance z-score was +1.49 in 2009, dipped during sparse 2012–2015 snapshots, recovered to +1.50 in 2013 and +1.18 in 2023. The altruism facet followed a similar arc—above-peer z-scores from 2015 to 2018 ('We're determined to build a better, more connected world for everyone'), then settling back to near-average by 2023–2024 as the copy became more internally focused on craft and speed.

The 2022–2023 pages introduced notably direct performance expectations: 'We expect Facebook employees to avoid wasting time on minor issues and focus on truly big challenges' and 'We push ourselves to ship things that are not just good, but also awe-inspiring.' This is a harder edge than the earlier 'move fast and break things' era, which framed speed as liberating rather than obligatory.

sections.heading: The DEI Arc: Rise, Peak, and Retreat
sections.body:
Diversity and inclusion language was essentially absent from the careers pages through 2012. It appeared in aspirational-vague form in 2013 ('We're dedicated to creating an environment where people can be their authentic selves') and grew steadily through 2016–2018, when belonging-culture registers appeared ('Be your authentic self. We're dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone belongs').

The sharpest expansion came in 2020–2021, when the pages devoted substantial space to employee resource groups (Women@, Pride@, Native@, Interfaith@, Latin@), explicit representation commitments ('We are dedicated to building a team that reflects the diversity of the people, all around the globe'), and direct leadership quotes on accountability. Inclusion z-scores hit +1.83 (2020) and +1.60 (2021)—well above peers.

By 2022 the copy began contracting. The 2023–2024 snapshots are thin (2 chunks each, flagged as such) and carry only belonging-culture framing with no explicit demographic or structural-process language. The 2025 page restores some inclusion copy ('Inclusion strengthens our workplace — and our world') but at a more generic, aspirational register. The 2026 snapshot—dominated by product descriptions of AR glasses and Llama—shows an inclusion z-score of –2.06 and zero DEI register hits across all categories. Readers should treat 2026 as a product-showcase page rather than a full careers page, so the signal is noisy, but the directional retreat from 2020–2021 highs is consistent across 2022–2025 as well.

sections.heading: The Techno-Optimism Pivot (2025–2026)
sections.body:
Techno-optimism scores were near zero or negative for most of the 2011–2022 period—the copy leaned on human connection and social mission rather than technology as an end in itself. That changed sharply in 2025 (z-score +1.85) and 2026 (+2.70), with the pages now leading on hardware specifics: 'Meta Quest headsets, AR wearables and Ray-Ban AI glasses,' 'AI is influencing the metaverse in mind-blowing ways,' and 'At the forefront of innovation, the possibilities are endless.'

This shift coincides with the altruism and DEI scores falling back toward or below peer averages. The 2025–2026 copy is less about connecting humanity and more about building frontier technology—a meaningful reframe of what Meta says it is recruiting for. Candidates drawn by the earlier 'build social value' framing should note that the current pages foreground AI and hardware ambition more than community or belonging.
